questions.question_text:
A curry recipe uses $4$ cups of vegetables for $6$ people.
How many cups are needed for $24$ people?

options.why: Added 24 people to four cups instead of keeping the quantities separate and scaling the recipe.
Used one cup per person and ignored that four cups serve six people.
Multiplied four cups by 24 people without first finding the number of recipe batches.

questions.question_text:
A bus travels $156$ km in $3$ hours at a steady rate.
How far will it travel in $7$ hours?

options.why: Multiplied the three-hour distance by seven without first finding the distance per hour.
Found 52 kilometres per hour but multiplied by the four additional hours only.
Found the hourly rate but stopped before multiplying it by seven hours.

questions.question_text:
A packaging line seals $84$ bags every $4$ minutes.
How many bags will it seal in $15$ minutes?

options.why: Multiplied 84 by 15 without dividing by the four-minute time block.
Multiplied 84 by the given four minutes rather than finding a one-minute rate.
Added 15 minutes to 84 bags instead of using the constant production rate.

questions.question_text:
A hire company earns $252$ dollars by renting identical kayaks at $18$ dollars each.
How many kayaks were rented?

options.why: Multiplied the total dollars by the price per kayak instead of dividing.
Stopped at 13 groups of 18, which account for only 234 dollars of the total.
Counted one extra group of 18, producing 270 dollars rather than 252 dollars.

questions.question_text:
Three cartons of fruit cost $27$ dollars.
At the same rate, how much do $8$ cartons cost?

options.why: Multiplied 27 dollars by eight without first finding the cost of one carton.
Added eight cartons to the given 27 dollars instead of applying a constant rate.
Doubled the three-carton cost as though eight cartons were only two groups of three.

questions.question_text:
A factory must make $1800$ parts.
A machine makes $60$ parts per hour and has already run for $18$ hours.
How many more hours are needed?

options.why: Found the time for all 1800 parts but did not subtract the 18 hours already worked.
Repeated the elapsed time instead of finding the production still remaining.
Added the 18 hours already worked to the 30-hour total rather than subtracting.
